_meta.law: source of truth for collections. a collection holds pages of one section (section field - pages live under pages/<section>/collections/). a multi-collection holds collections. engine: tools/build.py.

collections.title: The Complete Hitman
collections.caption: the four classic hits, 2002 to 2012, plus the console remasters that complete the line.
about: Four of the mainline Hitman games, covering the series' 2002-2012 decade: Silent Assassin, Contracts, Blood Money and Absolution. All four are still sold - the classics (2002-2006) DRM-free on Steam and GOG, Absolution on Steam. The wider lineage - Codename 47 (2000) and the World of Assassination line (2016-2023) - rides the series strip of every page as reference.

The classics run on and under the haswell iGPU bar and remain sold DRM-free. Absolution anchors the shelf with its 24 GB footprint. Where an official channel exists it comes first on the page; the archive routes sit next to it.

Two console remasters complete the picture, and neither shipped for windows: Hitman HD Trilogy (2013) remastered Silent Assassin, Contracts and Blood Money for PS3 and Xbox 360, and Hitman HD Enhanced Collection (2019) rebuilt Blood Money and Absolution at 4K/60 for PS4 and Xbox One. The windows builds on this shelf are therefore the definitive way to play these four on PC.
notes: Codename 47, the World of Assassination trilogy and the spin-offs (GO, Sniper, Sniper Challenge) sit outside the current catalogue; they appear in the series strips as reference only.

collections.title: The Complete Chicken Invaders
collections.caption: the complete line: five wars, their remasters written one by one, and the universe - 1999 to today.
about: The full Chicken Invaders line from InterAction studios: the five classic wars with every holiday release living as a version under its episode's page (four Christmas editions, two Easter editions, one Halloween, one Thanksgiving - switched from the dropdown, not scattered as standalone entries), plus the three things that complete the family: the per-episode remasters, the episodic rework, and Universe.

One production quirk stays on record: the third war's Christmas Edition (November 2006) shipped three months before the standard game (January 2007), making it the only edition in the series that predates its own episode.

InterAction studios is alive and every entry remains officially obtainable: the studio's download hub carries the classic line, Steam sells the mainline episodes and five of the eight holiday editions as DLC (the second and third wars' Christmas editions, the fourth war's Thanksgiving, and both fifth-war editions - the rest live on the studio's own store), and Universe is free to play. These pages are ownership stories, not rescues - the archive links ride along for preservation.

A sequel is never an upgrade, and the pages keep that law one war at a time: the first war's rebuild is Chicken Invaders Remastered (2023), the second war's is The Next Wave Remastered (2012), and the later wars ride the Episodes rework (2025) instead - no classic-engine remaster was ever made for wars three to five. Every classic page names its own rebuild, and every rebuild has its own page.
notes: The two remaster entries cover only their own war: Remastered (2023) is the first war's rebuild, The Next Wave Remastered (2012) is the second's. Episode 1: The Saga Begins is the new-engine remake of the first war, and the Episodes page carries the free rework line for wars two to five, version by version.

collections.title: The Dash Universe
collections.caption: PlayFirst's DinerTown empire: every Dash game of the pc era, one universe.
about: Diner Dash (2003) by gameLab and PlayFirst turned restaurant time-management into a franchise and its waitress Flo into a casual-gaming icon. The pc line it built runs a full decade: Restaurant Rescue (2006), Flo on the Go (2006), Hometown Hero (2007), Flo Through Time (2008) and Boom! (2010) carry the numbered story, and the formula spun off into whole sub-lines - Wedding Dash ran 2007-2010 across four games, Cooking Dash 2008-2010 across three, Hotel Dash 2009-2011 across two, and Avenue Flo (2009-2010) turned the waitress into a point-and-click adventurer.

The DinerTown side line filled out the town itself: Doggie, Dairy, Fashion, Parking, Fitness, Diaper and Garden Dash (2008-2011) moved the chained-service engine to spas, farms, studios, lots, gyms, daycares and gardens, DinerTown Tycoon (2009) stretched it into a business sim, and two licensed SpongeBob SquarePants crossovers (2006-2007) carried it onto Nickelodeon's turf. Twenty-seven titles, one universe, all of it the pc era.

The shelf's state is mixed and honest about it: seven of the twenty-seven still sell on Steam (Hometown Hero, Cooking Dash, Wedding Dash 2, Hotel Dash: Suite Success, Fitness Dash, Diaper Dash and DinerTown Tycoon), while the rest died with their channels - PlayFirst folded into Glu Mobile in 2014, playfirst.com is gone, and the download portals closed with it. The un-buyable cases are the archive's rescue lane: no store, no key server, preserved anyway.

Scope law for this collection: windows builds only. The mobile free-to-play era that followed the classic line is outside this collection - those builds belong to phones, and phones are out of scope for this archive. Each entry below is its own dug page with its own sources, sizes and archive routes.
